newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs set to head down, first prop 129.73.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs set to head down, first prop 129.73.

text.p: June BTP futures were set to turn lower on Thursday, finding intial support at Wednesday's low of 129.73 but with further to go on the downside, technical analysts said.
"It's probably too early to be looking at a significant downward movement but in the short term it's looking a little bit threatened," said Jonh Ratcliffe, senior analyst at Technical Data here.
Ratcliffe said in the first instance the market would find support levels around 129.73 and then at 129.50, a low from May 14, but neither of these would be aggressively strong.
By 0952 GMT, June BTPs were down 0.44 at 130.01.
"The daily indicators seem to have turned a corner and do have a lot more to go, but whether this will result in sideways activity or outright losses remains to be seen," he said.
"The risk is for a little bit more downside, but there's a base in the market ahead of 129 the figure which is going to be very solid."

On the upside he pegged 130.40,45 as a reasonable resistance level. But he said the market would find it difficult to make new highs because there was no significant level between 130.40 and the highs above 131.40 touched earlier in the year.
"There's a big figure grey area and until it gets to the top of that, selling rallies is going to be the pattern for at least the next couple of days," Ratcliffe said.

Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in a client note to look for further declines below the daily uptrend, currently at 129.94, to 38 percent retracement at 129.25 and to test wave structure support at 129.05.
"A confirmation of yesterday's break lower will virtually rule out a recovery to the weekly continuation high at 132.38," they said.
By 1000 GMT, June Eurolira was unchanged at 93.38.
